title.en: Rahab Hides the Spies and Hangs the Scarlet Cord
title.zh: 喇哈藏探子懸朱紅線繩

region.en: Jericho, house in the city wall

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Two spies lodge in the house of Rahab the harlot on Jericho's wall; the king's men come for them, and she hides them under the flax on the roof. She confesses that the land's hearts have melted before Israel's God, and bargains for her family's lives; the spies seal it with a scarlet thread in her window. She becomes an ancestress in the royal line.
summary.zh: 二探子宿於耶利哥城牆上妓女喇哈之家；王之人來捉，她將他們藏於屋頂麻稓中。她自承此地人心因以色列的神消化，為全家族的性命討價；探子以朱紅線繩繫於窗上為記。她後列入王統譜系。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Rahab appears in Matthew's genealogy; counted among converts in rabbinic tradition.

passages.text: And she said unto the men: 'I know that the LORD hath given you the land... for we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt... for the LORD your God, He is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.'

She let them down by a cord through the window, 'for her house was in the side of the wall, and she dwelt upon the wall', and received the oath: 'Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window'. As long as her family stayed within the house, they would be safe; the army would blameless hold the covenant. Paraphrase of Joshua 2:15-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Jericho's Walls Fall at the Shofar Blast
title.zh: 角聲中耶利哥城牆倒塌

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The armed men circle the city once a day for six days, priests blowing rams' horns before the ark, the people silent. On the seventh day they circle seven times; 'when the priests blew with the trumpet... the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat.' Rahab's house alone stands spared, and the city is put under the ban (herem).
summary.zh: 持械者一日繞城一次，共六日，祭司抬約櫃吹羊角，百姓靜默。第七日繞城七次；「祭司吹角的時候……百姓大聲呼喊，城牆就塌陷」。唯喇哈之屋蒙存，全城被滅歸於「當滅之物」（禁令）。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The herem passages are discussed critically in modern scholarship; record states the text.

passages.text: And it came to pass at the seventh time, when the priests blew with the horns, Joshua said unto the people: 'Shout; for the LORD hath given you the city.' ... So the people shouted, and they blew with the horns; and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the horn, that the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, whereupon the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Joshua 6:16, 20 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: Achan's Loot and the Valley of Trouble
title.zh: 亞干的贓物與亞割谷

region.en: Ai and the valley of Achor, land of Canaan

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Israel is routed at Ai because one man kept back spoils under the ban. The tribes pass before the LORD tribe by tribe until Achan of Judah is singled out; he confesses to a Babylonish garment, silver, and gold buried in his tent. He and his household are stoned and burned in the valley of Achor — 'the valley of trouble' — named as a memorial of transgression under holy war law.
summary.zh: 以色列在艾城潰敗，因一人私藏當滅之物。支派逐一經過，亞干屬猶大被指出；他供認藏巴比倫衣服、銀金於帳內。他與全家被石擊火焚於亞割谷——「連累之谷」——為聖戰法下違命之記念。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Joshua said unto Achan: 'My son, give, I pray thee, glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and make confession unto Him; and tell me now what thou hast done; hide it not from me.' And Achan answered Joshua, and said: 'Of a truth I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel... When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish mantle, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them.'

title.en: The Gibeonites' Mouldy Bread Trick
title.zh: 基遍人的霉餅計

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Neighbouring Hivites of Gibeon send ambassadors in patched wineskins and mouldy bread, claiming to have come 'from a very far country'. Israel's leaders swear peace without asking the mouth of the LORD; three days later the trick is discovered, but the oath stands — the Gibeonites become perpetual hewers of wood and drawers of water 'for the house of my God'.
summary.zh: 附近基遍的希未人遣使者，帶補過的皮酒袋與發霉的餅，自稱「從極遠之地而來」。以色列首領未求耶和華的口便起誓立和；三日後詭計被識破，然誓言有效——基遍人成為永遠劈柴挑水的人，「為我神的殿」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And they went to Joshua unto the camp at Gilgal, and said unto him, and to the men of Israel: 'We are come from a far country; now therefore make ye a covenant with us.' And the men of Israel said unto the Hivites: 'Peradventure ye dwell among us; how shall we make a covenant with you?'

The ambassadors showed their bread — 'it was dry, and had become mouldy cakes' — and their patched wineskins and mended sandals as proof of a long journey. The men 'asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD' and made peace. Three days later Israel learned they were neighbours; Joshua summoned them and said: 'Wherefore have ye beguiled us?' The oath could not be broken, so they were made servants at the altar — wood and water 'for the house of my God'. Paraphrase of Joshua 9:12-27 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Sun, Stand Thou Still upon Gibeon
title.zh: 日頭啊，你要停在基遍

region.en: Gibeon and the valley of Aijalon

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Five Amorite kings besiege Gibeon for its treaty with Israel; the LORD hurls great stones from heaven. In the middle of the battle Joshua speaks to the sun and the moon — 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed... and hastened not to go down about a whole day.'
summary.zh: 五亞摩利王因基遍與以色列立約而攻之；耶和華自天降大冰雹。戰中雅各向日月發言——「日頭啊，你要停在基遍；月亮啊，你要止在亞雅崙谷。日頭果然停住，月亮止住……不急速下落，約有一日之久。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Cross-cluster 'sun captured' motif.

passages.text: Then spoke Joshua to the LORD in the day when the LORD delivered up the Amorites before the children of Israel; and he said in the sight of Israel: 'Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon.' And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies... And there was no day like that before it or after it, that the LORD hearkened unto the voice of a man; for the LORD fought for Israel.

title.en: Caleb's Eighty-Five-Year Claim on Hebron
title.zh: 迦勒八十五歲索希伯崙

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Forty-five years after spying out the land, Caleb comes to Gilgal to claim Moses' oath: 'because I wholly followed the LORD my God'. Though 'as strong this day as... in the day that Moses sent me', he asks the hill country where the Anakim — the very giants that scared the other spies — still dwell, and takes Hebron for his inheritance: 'Give me this mountain.'
summary.zh: 窺地四十五年後，迦勒到吉甲索摩西的誓言：「因為我專心跟從耶和華我的神」。雖「今日我還是強壯，像摩西打發我去的那天」，他求的卻是亞衲族人——當年嚇退探子的巨人——仍居的山地，得希伯崙為業：「求你將耶和華那日應許我的這山給我。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And now, behold, the LORD hath kept me alive, as He spoke, these forty and five years... And now, behold, I am this day fourscore and five years old. As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, and to go out and to come in. Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the LORD spoke in that day.

title.en: Choose You This Day: Joshua's Covenant Assembly at Shechem
title.zh: 今日就可以選擇：示劍立約大會

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Old and old, Joshua gathers all Israel at Shechem and rehearses history from Terah's migration to the crossing of the Jordan. Then the charter choice: 'choose you this day whom ye will serve... but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.' The people answer that they will serve the LORD, who has done 'all these great things'; Joshua writes the words in the book of the law of God and sets up a great stone under the terebinth as witness.
summary.zh: 年老的約書亞召集以色列眾人於示劍，數說歷史——自他拉遷徙至過約旦河。隨後是根本抉擇：「今日就可以選擇所要事奉的……至於我和我家，我們必定事奉耶和華。」百姓應允事奉行「這一切大事」的神；約書亞將話寫在神的律法書上，立一塊大石頭在橡樹下作見證。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD. And the people answered and said: 'Far be it from us that we should forsake the LORD, to serve other gods.'

title.en: Ehud the Left-Handed and the Dagger for Eglon
title.zh: 左撇子以笏與刺伊磯倫之劍

region.en: Palace of Eglon at Jericho (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 伊磯倫王宮，耶利哥（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Moab oppresses Israel eighteen years. Ehud, a left-handed Benjamite, makes a two-edged dagger a cubit long and straps it to his right thigh; having delivered tribute to the very fat king Eglon, he returns alone on the pretext of 'a secret errand', and drives the blade — handle and all — into the king's belly while the servants, thinking their master covers his feet, wait respectfully outside. Israel then holds the fords of the Jordan.
summary.zh: 摩押壓制以色列十八年。便雅憫人左手便利的以笏打造一把兩刃劍長一肘，綁在右腿上；獻貢後藉口「奉王命說機密話」獨自返回，將劍——連柄帶刃——刺入極肥胖的伊磯倫王腹中；僕人以為王正在解衣，恭立門外。以色列隨即把守約旦渡口。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Ehud put forth his left hand, and took the sword from his right thigh, and thrust it into his belly; and the haft also went in after the blade; and the fat closed upon the blade, for he drew not the sword out of his belly; and it came out behind.

Ehud escaped past the quarries, sounded the shofar in the hill country of Ephraim, and came down after the people of Israel; he said: 'Follow after me; for the LORD hath delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.' They seized the fords of the Jordan and slew about ten thousand Moabites, 'every lusty man, and every man of valour; and there escaped not a man. So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel; and the land had rest fourscore years.' Paraphrase of Judges 3:26-30 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Deborah, Barak, and the Chariots of Hazor
title.zh: 底波拉巴拉克與夏瑣戰車

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Deborah the prophetess judges Israel under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel. She summons Barak: 'Hath not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded thee... draw toward mount Tabor?' Barak will go only if she goes; she agrees — 'for the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour'. Sisera's nine hundred iron chariots are swept away by the flooded Kishon, and the general himself falls by a woman's hand.
summary.zh: 女先知底波拉在拉瑪伯特利之間的棕樹下治理以色列。她召巴拉：「耶和華以色列的神豈沒有吩咐你……往他泊山去？」巴拉說你若不同去就不去；她應允——「你行的路必得不著榮耀」。西西拉的九百輛鐵車被漲溢的基順河沖去，主帥親自倒在婦人手中。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Barak said unto her: 'If thou wilt go with me, then I will go; but if thou wilt not go with me, I will not go.' And she said: 'I will surely go with thee; notwithstanding, the journey that thou takest shall not be for thine honour; for the LORD will give Sisera over into the hand of a woman.'

Barak went down from Tabor with ten thousand men; the LORD discomfited Sisera and all his chariots with the edge of the sword, and Sisera alighted from his chariot and fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite. Deborah and Barak pursued the discomfited army to Harosheth — 'and there was not a man left'. Paraphrase of Judges 4:14-16 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Jael, the Milk, and the Tent-Pin
title.zh: 雅億、奶與帳棚橛

region.en: Tent of Heber the Kenite, plain of Esdraelon
region.zh: 基尼人希百之帳棚，以斯德倫平原

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Fleeing on foot, Sisera seeks refuge in Jael's tent. She covers him with a rug, gives him milk instead of the water he asks, and waits until he is asleep; then she takes the workman's hammer and a tent-pin and drives it through his temple into the ground. Barak arrives in pursuit — 'and, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the pin was in his temple'. The Song of Deborah crowns her 'most blessed above women in the tent'.
summary.zh: 徒步逃亡的西西拉入雅億帳中求庇。她以毯蒙他，給他奶而非所求的水，待他睡熟；便取工人的錘與帳棚橛，穿透他的太陽穴釘入地中。巴拉追至——「西西拉已死倒臥，橛子在他鬢邊」。底波拉之歌稱她「帳棚中的婦人比眾婦人何等有福」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: But Jael the wife of Heber took a tent-pin, and took a hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the pin into his temples, and fastened it into the ground; for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died. And, behold, as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him: 'Come, and I will show thee the man whom thou seekest.' And he came unto her; and, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the pin was in his temples.

title.en: Awake, Awake, Deborah: The Song of Victory
title.zh: 底波拉啊醒起：得勝之歌

region.en: Ramah and Bethel, judge's palm tree
region.zh: 拉瑪與伯特利，士師的棕樹

texts.period: Composed c. 11th-10th c. BCE (archaic Hebrew, among the oldest strata of the Hebrew Bible); recorded in Judges 5; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: One of the oldest poems in the Hebrew Bible: Deborah and Barak sing that 'when the people offer themselves willingly, bless ye the LORD', rehearse the march of the tribes, curse Meroz for not helping, and crown the battle with Jael's act — 'At her feet he bowed, he fell, he lay.'
summary.zh: 希伯來聖經最古老詩歌之一：底波拉與巴拉唱「百姓甘心犧牲自己之處，你們當稱頌耶和華」，歷數各支派行軍，咒詛未來助戰的米羅斯，以雅億之舉收束——「在她腳前他屈身、仆倒、躺臥」。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Judges 5's archaic language places it among the oldest biblical texts (cf. Song of the Sea).

passages.text: Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam on that day, saying: 'When men let grow their hair in Israel, when the people offer themselves willingly, bless ye the LORD! Hear, O ye kings; give ear, O ye princes; I, unto the LORD will I sing; I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.'

The poem remembers the Lord going forth from Seir, the earth trembling, the heavens dropping, 'even yon Sinai at the presence of the LORD'; the people volunteered to the battle, Ephraim behind Amalek, Benjamin among the peoples, princes of Machir, Zebulun risking their lives, Naphtali on the heights. The Kishon swept the enemy away: 'the river Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon. O my soul, march on with strength!' Paraphrase of Judges 5:4-21 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Gideon's Fleece of Wool
title.zh: 基甸的羊毛神蹟

region.zh: 俄弗拉，約阿施的打麥場

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The angel of the LORD finds the youngest son of Joash threshing wheat in a winepress 'to hide it from the Midianites': 'The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.' Gideon demands signs — first dew on the fleece only, then dry fleece in wet grass — and destroys his father's altar of Baal by night. His father defends him with the classic put-down: 'Will ye plead for Baal? If he be a god, let him plead for himself.'
summary.zh: 耶和華的使者見約阿施幼子在酒醡裡打麥，「為要防備米甸人」：「大能的勇士啊，耶和華與你同在。」基甸求兆——先羊毛獨有露，後草地有露羊毛獨乾——並夜間拆毀其父的巴力壇。其父以名句護子：「你們是為巴力爭論麼？他若是神，讓他為自己爭論吧。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Jerubbaal, 'let Baal plead', becomes Gideon's by-name.

passages.text: And it was so: for he rose up early on the morrow, and pressed the flock together, and put the fleece with the dew on the ground only, and there was dew on all the ground, but on the fleece there was not dew. ... Then Gideon said unto God: 'Let not Thine anger be kindled against me, and I will speak but this once: let me make trial, I pray Thee, but this once with the fleece; let there now be dew on the fleece only, and upon all the ground let there be dry.'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 6:38-39 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis; second sign (dry fleece) combined.

title.en: Three Hundred with Trumpets, Torches, and Jars
title.zh: 三百人持號角火把與瓶

region.en: Spring of Harod, valley of Jezreel

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Thirty-two thousand volunteers are reduced by the LORD's own vetting: first the fearful depart — twenty-two thousand; then the three hundred who lap water like dogs are chosen against a Midianite army 'like locusts'. Armed with trumpets, empty jars, and torches, they surround the camp by night, break the jars at Gideon's signal, and cry 'The sword of the LORD and of Gideon!' The Midianites flee; the sword is 'of the LORD', and the battle turns on noise and light.
summary.zh: 三萬二千志願者經神親自篩減：先懼怕者離去——兩萬二千人；再以舔水如狗的三百人對陣「如同蝗蟲」的米甸大軍。他們以號角空瓶火把夜間圍營，在基甸號令下碎瓶，呼「耶和華和基甸的刀！」米甸人潰逃；刀屬耶和華，戰事成於聲與光。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the three companies blew the horns, and broke the pitchers, and held the torches in their left hands, and the horns in their right hands to blow withal; and they cried: 'The sword of the LORD and of Gideon!' And they stood every man in his place round about the camp; and all the host ran; and they shouted, and put them to flight.

title.en: Abimelech and the Talking Bramble
title.zh: 亞比米勒與會說話的荊棘

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Gideon's son by a Shechemite concubine slays his seventy brothers on one stone and is made king. Jotham, the lone survivor, pronounces the fable of the trees from Mount Gerizim — olive, fig, vine, all refusing kingship, until the bramble accepts with threats of fire — 'and let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon'. The curse works itself out: Abimelech and Shechem destroy each other, and he dies with a millstone-brain wound, begging his armour-bearer to finish him.
summary.zh: 基甸示劍婢所生之子在一塊石上殺七十弟兄而為王。倖存的約坦自基利心山發言樹木寓言——橄欖、無花果、葡萄皆拒王位，直至荊棘以火相脅而受——「願火從荊棘裡出來，燒滅利巴嫩的香柏樹」。咒詛應驗：亞比米勒與示劍同歸於盡，他被磨石擊傷腦，求拿兵器的少年刺死。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Judges 9:56-57 renders the Shechem bloodguilt as divine repayment.

passages.text: And the bramble said unto the trees: 'If in truth ye anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shadow; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.' ... When Abimelech had fought against the city all that day, he took the city, and slew the people that was therein; and he beat down the city, and sowed it with salt.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 9:15, 45 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

passages.text: At Thebez a woman cast an upper millstone on Abimelech's head and broke his skull; he called hastily to his armour-bearer, 'Draw thy sword and slay me, that men say not of me: A woman slew him', 'and his young man thrust him through, and he died'. 'Thus did God requite the wickedness of Abimelech, which he did unto his father, in slaying his seventy brethren.' Paraphrase of Judges 9:50-56 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.

title.en: Jephthah's Vow and His Only Child
title.zh: 耶弗他的誓言與獨女

region.zh: 基列的米斯巴，約旦河東

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The outcast son of a harlot is recalled to lead Gilead against Ammon, and vows: 'Whatsoever cometh forth from the doors of my house to meet me... shall surely be the LORD's, and I will offer it up for a burnt-offering.' He wins the war — 'with a very great slaughter' — and returns to Mizpah, where his only daughter comes dancing with timbrels. Two months she bewails her maidenhood in the mountains; 'and it came to pass at the end of two months, that he did with her according to his vow', and Israel's daughters lament her yearly.
summary.zh: 妓女之子被逐者受召領基列抗亞捫，起誓：「我從我家門口迎接我回來的……必歸耶和華，我也必將他獻為燔祭。」他大敗亞捫——「殺戮甚大」——回到米斯巴，獨女擊鼓跳舞出迎。她於山中兩月哀哭處女之身；「兩月已滿，他照所許的願行了」，以色列女子年年為她哀哭。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Rabbinic tradition debates whether the vow was fulfilled by sacrifice or perpetual virginity; the narrative itself is stark.

passages.text: And when he saw her, he rent his clothes, and said: 'Alas, my daughter! thou hast brought me very low, and thou art among them that trouble me; for I have opened my mouth unto the LORD, and I cannot go back.' And she said unto him: 'My father, thou hast opened thy mouth unto the LORD; do unto me according to that which hath proceeded out of thy mouth.'

title.en: A Nazirite Announced: Samson's Birth
title.zh: 拿細耳人的預告：參孫出生

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The angel of the LORD appears to the barren wife of Manoah: 'thou shalt conceive, and bear a son; and no razor shall come on his head; for the child shall be a Nazirite unto God from the womb'. Manoah asks his name and receives only: 'Why askest thou thus after my name, seeing it is hidden?' The angel ascends in the flame of the altar; the child is born and 'the LORD blessed him', named Samson.
summary.zh: 耶和華的使者向瑪挪亞不育之妻顯現：「你必懷孕生一個兒子；不可用剃刀剃他的頭，因為這孩子從母腹裡就歸神作拿細耳人。」瑪挪亞問其名，只答：「你何必問我的名，我名是奇妙的？」使者在壇上火燄中升去；孩子出生，「耶和華賜福與他」，名參孫。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Nazirite rules (Num 6) frame the hero's taboo.

passages.text: And Manoah said unto the angel of the LORD: 'What is thy name, that when thy words come to pass we may do thee honour?' And the angel of the LORD said unto him: 'Wherefore askest thou after my name, seeing it is hidden?' So Manoah took the kid with the meal-offering, and offered it upon the rock unto the LORD; and the angel did wondrously... and the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar.

title.en: Honey in the Lion: Samson's Wedding Riddle
title.zh: 獅中之蜜：參孫的婚宴謎語

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: On the road to his Philistine bride a young lion roars at Samson; the spirit of the LORD comes on him and he tears it 'as he would have rent a kid'. Later he finds honey in the carcass. At the seven-day feast he bets thirty linen garments on a riddle: 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness.' The bride is bullied into betraying the answer; Samson's reply — 'If ye had not plowed with my heifer' — is itself a riddle, and he pays the debt by slaying thirty men of Ashkelon.
summary.zh: 往非利士新娘路上，獅子吼叫向參孫；耶和華的靈感動他，他撕裂獅子「如同撕裂山羊羔」。後在屍內得蜜。七日婚宴上他以三十件裡衣外衣賭一謎語：「喫的從喫者出來，甜的從強者出來。」新娘被逼供出答案；參孫的回話——「你們若非用我的母牛犢耕種」——本身又是一謎，遂殺亞實基倫三十人償債。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. The Nazirite touches a corpse — transgression woven into the hero cycle.

passages.text: And the men of the city said unto him on the seventh day before the sun went down: 'What is sweeter than honey? and what is stronger than a lion?' And he said unto them: 'If ye had not plowed with my heifer, ye had not found out my riddle.' And the spirit of the LORD came upon him mightily, and he went down to Ashkelon, and slew of them thirty men, and took their apparel, and gave changes of raiment unto them which expounded the riddle.

title.en: Foxes with Firebrands and the Jawbone of an Ass
title.zh: 帶火把的狐狸與驢腮骨

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Denied his wife, Samson catches three hundred foxes, turns them tail to tail with firebrands between, and lets them run through the standing corn of the Philistines. When they burn his wife and her father in revenge, he smites them 'hip and thigh with a great slaughter', then slays a thousand with the fresh jawbone of an ass, naming the place Ramath-lehi. Thirsty, he calls on God; water bursts from the hollow in Lehi.
summary.zh: 妻子被奪，參孫捉三百隻狐狸，尾尾相對，中間捆上火把，放入非利士人站著的禾稼。他們燒其妻與岳父報復，他便「大大殺敗他們，連腿帶腰」；後以未乾的驢腮骨殺千人，地名拉末利希。渴極呼神；神使利希的窪處裂開出水。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And he found a new jawbone of an ass, and put forth his hand, and took it, and slew a thousand men therewith. And Samson said: 'With the jawbone of an ass, heaps upon heaps; with the jawbone of an ass have I slain a thousand men.' ... And God clave the hollow place that was in Lehi, and there came water thereout; and when he had drunk, his spirit came again, and he revived.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 15:16, 19 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: Delilah's Loom: The Nazirite Sheared
title.zh: 大利拉的織機：剪斷拿細耳人

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The Philistine lords offer Delilah eleven hundred shekels for Samson's secret. Three times he mocks her — green withs, new ropes, the weaver's beam — and each test fails while she cries 'thou hast mocked me'. At last, 'pressed daily with her words', he tells her of the Nazirite vow, and she begins to weaken him. His head is shaved on her knees; the LORD departs from him; the Philistines put out his eyes and set him to grind in the prison at Gaza.
summary.zh: 非利士首領許大利拉一千一百舍客勒買參孫的秘密。三次他戲弄她——青繩、新繩、織機的緯線——試而皆敗，她哭「你欺哄我」。末了，因「天天催逼，甚至他心裡煩悶要死」，他說出拿細耳人之願；她開始消磨他。頭髮在她膝上被剃；耶和華離開他；非利士人剜其目，在迦薩監裡推磨。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And she said unto him: 'How canst thou say, I love thee, when thy heart is not with me? thou hast mocked me these three times, and hast not told me wherein thy great strength lieth.' And it came to pass, when she pressed him daily with her words, and urged him, that his soul was vexed unto death; and he told her all his heart, and said unto her: 'There hath not come a razor upon my head; for I have been a Nazirite unto God from my mother's womb; if I be shaven, then my strength will go from me, and I shall become weak, and be like any other man.'

title.en: Between the Pillars: Samson's Death at the Feast of Dagon
title.zh: 雙柱之間：參孫死於大袞之宴

region.zh: 大袞神廟，迦薩（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: The Philistine lords celebrate their god Dagon for delivering Samson and summon the blinded prisoner 'to make sport'. Between the two central pillars the boy leads him, and he prays: 'O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray Thee, and strengthen me, I pray Thee, only this once'. Pushing with all his might he brings the house down on the lords and all the people — 'so the dead which he slew at his death were more than they which he slew in his life' — and his brothers bury him between Zorah and Eshtaol.
summary.zh: 非利士首領聚集宴大袞，慶其神將仇敵交在手中，召盲囚「戲耍」。童子引他立於兩根中柱之間，他禱告：「主耶和華啊，求你眷念我，求你賜我這一次的力量。」盡力推之，房屋倒塌在首領與眾人身上——「他死時所殺的人比活著所殺的還多」——其兄弟將他葬於瑣拉以實陶之間。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And Samson called unto the LORD, and said: 'O Lord GOD, remember me, I pray Thee, and strengthen me, I pray Thee, only this once, O God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.' And Samson took hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house rested, and leaned upon them, the one with his right hand, and the other with his left. And Samson said: 'Let me die with the Philistines.' And he bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell upon the lords, and upon all the people that were therein.

title.en: Micah's Silvered Idol and the Danite Theft
title.zh: 米迦的鍍銀神像與但人竊像

region.en: House of Micah in Ephraim; Laish in the far north
region.zh: 以法蓮的米迦之家；極北的拉億

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: Micah restores stolen silver to his mother, who dedicates it to a graven image and a molten one; Micah makes a house of gods, an ephod, and ordains his own son priest. A wandering Levite is hired as priest 'for ten pieces of silver a year'. Then five Danite spies, and afterwards six hundred armed men, take the image and the Levite — who goes over gladly — and fall on peaceful Laish, renaming it Dan. 'In those days there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes.'
summary.zh: 米迦歸還所竊之銀給母親，母親以之鑄成像；米迦設神堂、製以弗得、立己子為祭司。又僱流浪利未人「每年十舍客勒銀子」為祭司。五個但支派探子，繼而六百帶刀者，奪像與利未人——利未人欣然從之——攻陷安居的拉億，改名但。「那時以色列中沒有王，各人任意而行。」

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917.

passages.text: And the five men that went to spy out the land went up, and came in thither, and took the graven image, and the ephod, and the teraphim, and the molten image; and the priest stood in the entering of the gate with the six hundred men that were girt with weapons of war. ... And they said unto him: 'Hold thy peace, lay thine hand upon thy mouth, and go with us, and be to us a father and a priest; is it better for thee to be priest unto the house of one man, or that thou be priest unto a tribe and a family in Israel?'
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 18:17, 19 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

title.en: The Outrage at Gibeah: A Levite and His Concubine
title.zh: 基便之惡：利未人與其妾

texts.period: Composite narrative, composed c. 8th-6th c. BCE; principal MS: Leningrad Codex B19a (1008 CE)

summary.en: A Levite's concubine plays the harlot and flees to her father's house; he follows and wins her back. Crossing Benjamin by night, no man takes them in until an old man of Gibeah does. The wicked men of the city surround the house 'that we may know him'; the host and the Levite offer the women; the concubine is thrust out and dies at the door. The Levite cuts her into twelve pieces and sends a piece to every tribe of Israel — the call to arms that nearly exterminates Benjamin.
summary.zh: 利未人的妾行淫歸父家；他前往勸回。夜過便雅憫地，無人接宿，直至基比亞一老人。城中匪徒圍屋「我們要與他交合」；主人與利未人皆出女子；妾被推出，死於門前。利未人將她切成十二塊，使人拿著傳送以色列四境——號召各支派，幾乎滅盡便雅憫。

sensitivity.note: Canonical scripture of a living tradition; quoted from public-domain JPS 1917. Text contains sexual violence; stated through the narrative's own voice without dramatization.

passages.text: And it came to pass at midnight, that the woman came to the door of the house of her father-in-law, and fell down; there she lay till the light of the morning. ... And her master rose up in the morning, and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way; and, behold, the woman his concubine was fallen down at the door of the house, with her hands upon the threshold.
passages.note: Verbatim: JPS 1917, Judges 19:26-27 (public domain), condensed with ellipsis.

passages.text: He laid her on the ass and journeyed home; then he took a knife and cut her, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her into all the coasts of Israel with the message: 'Consider it, take counsel, and speak.' All Israel gathered 'as one man, from Dan even to Beer-sheba' — the narrative that leads to the war of Benjamin. Paraphrase of Judges 19:29-30; 20:1 (JPS 1917); not verbatim.
